witness_description: On Ω=(0,1] with Lebesgue probability, let A_n=(0,1/n] for every integer n≥1. Then P(A_n)=1/n→0, ∑_{n=1}^∞P(A_n) is the divergent harmonic series, and A_n i.o.=∅, so P(A_n i.o.)=0.
refutation_explanation: The events are decreasing and every x∈(0,1] belongs to only finitely many of them: choose N>1/x, then x∉A_n for n≥N. Thus their limsup is empty even though their probabilities have divergent sum, contradicting the claimed conclusion 1.
search_space: All 20 pairs (a,b) with a∈{1,2,3,4} and b∈{0,1,2,3,4}, representing A_n=(0,1/(a n+b)] on (0,1] for n≥1, checked in lexicographic order; the first certified witness is (a,b)=(1,0).
